chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Mu'awiya ibn Wahb, from Sa'id al-Samman who said: I was in the presence of

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), when two men from the Zaydiites came to him. They said: 'Is there among you an Imam whose obedience is obligatory?' He said: 'No.' The narrator then said they claimed: 'The trustworthy ones have informed us from you that you issue fatwas, acknowledge it and speak accordingly, and we can name them to you — so-and-so and so-and-so — they are people of piety and diligence, from among those who do not lie.' Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) became angry and said: 'I did not command them to this!' When they saw the anger in his face, they went out. He said to me: 'Do you know these two?' I said: 'Yes, they are both from the people of our market, from the Zaydiites, and they allege that the sword of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) is with Abdullah ibn al-Hasan.' He said: 'They lied — may Allah curse them! By Allah, Abdullah ibn al-Hasan has not seen it with his two eyes, not with one of his eyes, nor has his father seen it — O Allah! — unless he saw it with Ali ibn al-Husain (peace be upon him). If they were truthful, what is the mark on its hilt? And what is the trace at its striking-place? Indeed with me is the sword of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), and with me is the banner of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), his armour, his equipment and his helmet. If they were truthful, what

is the mark on the armour of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family)? And with me is the victorious banner of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), and with me are the Tablets of Moses and his Staff, and with me is the ring of Solomon son of David (peace be upon them both), and with me is the basin in which Moses (peace be upon him) used to offer the sacrifice. And with me is the Name which the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), whenever he placed it between the Muslims and the polytheists, no arrow would reach from the polytheists to the Muslims. And with me is the like of what the angels brought, and the example of the weapons among us is like the example of the Ark among the Children of Israel. The Children of Israel were such that

whichever household the Ark was found to be upon their doors was given prophethood, and whoever from us the weapons come to is given the Imamate. My father wore the armour of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) and it trailed on the ground, and I wore it and it was (too large), and our Qa'im is he who when he wears it, it will fill him — if Allah wills.

key_terms.التَّابُوت: The Ark — the Ark of the Covenant in Israelite tradition, used as an analogy for the Imami weapons
key_terms.الثِّقَاتُ: The trustworthy ones — reliable transmitters or companions
key_terms.الزَّيْدِيَّةِ: The Zaydiites — followers of Zayd ibn Ali, who held that any descendant of Fatima who rose in armed revolt could be Imam
key_terms.السِّلَاح: The weapons/arms — here referring specifically to the sacred relics inherited by the Imams as signs of authority
key_terms.الْقَائِم: The Qa'im — the rising/standing one, referring to the awaited Imam al-Mahdi
key_terms.الْمِغْلَبَة: The victorious (banner) — a title for the Prophet's standard that brought victory in battle
key_terms.مُفْتَرَضُ الطَّاعَةِ: Imam whose obedience is obligatory — a theological term used in Shia discourse to denote the divinely-appointed Imam

ai.seo_question: What sacred relics and prophetic weapons does Imam al-Sadiq claim to possess as proof of his Imamate?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) responds to two Zaydi visitors who challenged him about claiming the Imamate, by asserting that he possesses the sacred relics of the Prophet (swords, armour, banner) as well as divine artifacts from earlier prophets (Moses's tablets and staff, Solomon's ring), and establishes that possession of the prophetic weapons is a sign of legitimate Imamate — just as possession of the Ark was the sign of prophethood among the Children of Israel. He concludes by prophesying that the Qa'im (the twelfth Imam) will be the one whose body perfectly fills the Prophet's armour.
